methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece explicitly identifies the concentration problem: while data center infrastructure concentrates in NoVA, small-business AI adoption—the mechanism for distribution—lags statewide, signaling a deepening capability gap rather than democratization.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Young workforce facing AI pressure without corresponding depth-building infrastructure suggests shallow adoption under duress rather than genuine capability development, positioning Richmond in reactive rather than proactive AI posture.

signals.title: Israeli AI maritime tech company joins Virginia Beach incubator - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: Israeli maritime AI firm joining Virginia Beach incubator demonstrates sector-specific deep capability development outside NoVA, signaling potential for distributed excellence through domain specialization in defense/maritime tech.

signals.title: Trump pushes data centers. That puts him in opposition to many of his supporters.
signals.signal_reading: Rural Republican opposition to data centers reveals infrastructure concentration benefiting metros while externalizing costs to rural areas—infrastructure without local capability-building widens rather than bridges the geographic AI divide.

signals.title: University of Virginia Students Help Businesses Explore AI - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: UVA students helping businesses explore AI represents peer-to-peer knowledge transfer mechanism that could enable distributed deep adoption if scaled beyond Charlottesville, though currently signals academic-led rather than grassroots distribution.
